title: Ticket booking: same seat sold twice
summary: A concert goes on sale and thousands of fans click the same VIP seats in the same second.
background: A ticketing site keeps one row per seat per event in event_seats with a status of free or sold. When a fan clicks buy, the server finds the first free VIP seat, waits for the payment gateway, then marks the seat sold and writes a booking.

The naive flow reads a free seat with a plain SELECT. Twenty fans run that SELECT at the same moment, all of them get the same first free seat, and all of them write a booking for it. The seat is sold many times and the venue has angry fans at the door.

The fix is to claim the seat and change it in one statement: UPDATE event_seats SET status = 'sold' WHERE (event_id, seat_id) = (SELECT ... WHERE status = 'free' ORDER BY seat_id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING seat_id. FOR UPDATE locks the chosen row, SKIP LOCKED makes other fans jump to the next free seat instead of waiting in line, and because the row is updated Postgres re-checks status = 'free' on the newest version. A unique constraint on bookings (event_id, seat_id) is the last line of defense.

race.goal: Event 1 has 8 free VIP seats. 20 fans try to buy one seat each. Exactly 8 bookings may exist and no seat may have two bookings.

inner.title: Who sits where
inner.prompt: Join bookings, customers, events and seats to print the ticket of every booking.

left.title: Tickets sold per event, including zero
left.prompt: List every event with its number of bookings. Events with no booking must show 0.

right.title: Seat map of an event
right.prompt: For event 2 list every seat with the customer holding it or NULL when it is still free.

full.title: Customers versus newsletter
full.prompt: Match customers with newsletter subscribers by email, keeping customers who never subscribed and subscribers who never bought.

cross.title: Event x section grid
cross.prompt: Build every event x seat section pair and count how many seats of that section each event sold.

self.title: Referral chain
self.prompt: Show every customer next to the customer who referred them.

semi.title: Customers who went to Lisbon
semi.prompt: Return the customers with at least one booking for an event in a Lisbon venue.

anti.title: Events with no sales
anti.prompt: Return the events that have no booking at all.

lateral.title: Latest booking per customer
lateral.prompt: For every customer return the most recent booking with the event title.
